text.p: These are the leading stories in Pakistani newspapers on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Pakistan has arranged a loan of $500 million by floating $300 million worth of Eurobonds and securitisation of Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd shares worth about $200 million.
- The All Pakistan Textile Mills Association has suggested that sick units beyond redemption should be liquidated.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has issued new procedures to be followed by banks in handling export of gold jewellery.
- The government has increased annual registration and licence fees for hotels, restaurants and travel agents.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif vowed to end horse-trading through a constitutional amendment which would also do away with floor-crossing and blackmailing in politics.
- The Foreign Office said all 13 officials of the Pakistani consulate in Mazar-i-Sharif had been evacuated.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The government has levied regulatory duty ranging from 10 to 35 percent ad valorem on 71 items with effect from May 30.
- British Airways has initiated its first cargo freighter service from Lahore to London.
FINANCIAL POST
- The government has earned an additional revenue of 700 million rupees through transparent auction of the textile quota.
THE NEWS
- The Senate (upper house) passed a new accountability law amid opposition protests.

- The government has decided to accord the status of opposition leader in the National Assembly (lower house) to Pakistan People's Party chairperson Benazir Bhutto whose party was routed in the February 3 election this year.
- Pakistan's trade gap will increase to $4 billion due to a continous decline in exports.
- Pakistani and U.S. troops will carry out joint exercises in Punjab and Sindh provinces in June.
THE NATION
- The government has offered full financial support to Benazir Bhutto for filing a law suit against the Sunday Express for alleging that she had bought a mansion in Surrey.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
